newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks tumble, end more than two pct lower.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks tumble, end more than two pct lower.

text.p: Tokyo stocks stumbled late in Wednesday afternoon trade to end more than two percent lower, rattled by comments by the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) deputy governor that the central bank is considering the right timing to raise the official discount rate, brokers said.
Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd, which was raided by prosecutors on Tuesday in a widening investigation into links between financial firms and racketeers, continued to fall, closing 70 yen lower at 1,320.

Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said on Wednesday that the ministry may take strict measures once the bank's role in the scandal involving Nomura Securities Co Ltd and "sokaiya" racketeers becomes clear.
Nikko Securities Co Ltd fell 27 yen to 691, on news that an affiliate conducted illegal bond trades and that the ministry was likely to impose penalties on the affiliate.
Brokers said that, although the news was worrying, so far the damage was limited to Nikko itself and was not greatly affecting the brokerage sector or the overall market.
Declining sectors were headed by rubber, fisheries, automobiles, pulp/paper and trading houses.
The gas sector, managing to defy the Nikkei average's drop, was the only sector posting major gains.

The most heavily traded issue on the first section of the Tokyo bourse was Tokyo Gas Co Ltd, which rose 11 yen to end at 319 on turnover of 13.47 million shares. Brokers said that a strong yen would cut the firm's procurement costs.
It was followed by major trading house Nissho Iwai Corp with 12.48 million shares, which added 15 yen to end at 480 due to strong earnings.
Total turnover was 436 million shares, little changed from the Tuesday session. Losers beat winners 886 issues to 245, while 121 issues were unchanged.
Other indices were down, with the broader TOPIX off 27.57 points or 1.83 percent to finish at 1,475.99. The Nikkei 300 fell 5.93 points or 2.04 percent to 285.13.
The second section index slipped 13.94 points or 0.79 percent to 1,746.64.
Second section turnover was 12.95 million issues, up from 11.50 million on the previous day.
The over-the-counter index was down 4.46 points or 0.37 percent at 1,187.24.
